question.prompt:
Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is a rhombus with perimeter \(52\) meters. The length of diagonal \(\overline{AC}\) is \(24\) meters. What is the area in square meters of rhombus \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2019_AMC_8_Q04_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Draw the other diagonal \(BD\), and call its intersection with \(AC\) point \(M\). The diagonals of a rhombus bisect one another at right angles, producing four congruent right triangles.

[Figure 1](figures/2019_AMC_8_Q04_official_expansion_solution_fig1.png)

Each side of the rhombus is \(52/4=13\) meters, and \(AM=24/2=12\) meters. In right triangle \(ABM\), the side \(AB\) is the hypotenuse. The Pythagorean theorem gives

\[
BM^2=13^2-12^2=169-144=25,
\]

so \(BM=5\) meters. Each of the four right triangles has area \(\frac12\cdot12\cdot5=30\) square meters. Thus the rhombus has area \(4\cdot30=\boxed{120}\) square meters, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

The diagonals are useful because they turn the given side and diagonal lengths into a right-triangle calculation.
solutions.title: Use perpendicular rhombus diagonals and a 5-12-13 right triangle
